# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Managed agent execution with computer use (OpenAI Agents API)

**Category:** AI / Automation

**What happened?**
The Agents API now lets agents operate software through screens (click, type, navigate) with OpenAI managing the runtime, and brings in Codex's multi-agent features, tool search, tool calling and context compaction. Availability is via the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work (Pro 500, Enterprise).

**Why it matters?**
Computer use reaches systems that have no API (legacy admin panels, vendor portals). It also gives an agent a logged-in session, which is the credential risk we flagged on Oct 4. Hosted execution moves code and data to the vendor.

**Business Value:** Automates manual work in tools without integrations; fewer custom connectors.

**Company Relevance:** 55

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (revisit after we have an agent credential policy; pilot on one non-sensitive portal task)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

---

**Technology:** Cheap routing models (OpenAI Decisions API, limited preview)

**Category:** AI / Engineering

**What happened?**
A low-cost model returns one choice from a fixed list for text or image input. Broad release was announced for "the coming days" (not yet confirmed).

**Why it matters?**
Most agent cost goes to calls that only decide (classify a ticket, pick a next step). Routing those to the cheapest model can cut spend and latency without touching quality on hard tasks. The same pattern works with any vendor's small model.

**Business Value:** Lower inference bills; faster triage and routing.

**Company Relevance:** 62

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Pilot (test the pattern with any small model, not only OpenAI's)

**Expected Impact:** Short

---

**Technology:** Multi-model tool platforms (GitHub Copilot with Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash)

**Category:** Developer Tools

**What happened?**
GitHub added Claude Fable 5.1 (Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (all paid tiers) to Copilot. Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusions; the Copilot harness is generally available in JetBrains.

**Why it matters?**
A single seat now gives access to competing models, which weakens the case for paying several vendors for overlapping coding assistants, and content exclusions give a real data-boundary control.

**Business Value:** Seat consolidation; side-by-side model comparison on our own code.

**Company Relevance:** 66

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Pilot (a two-week bake-off on real tickets)

**Expected Impact:** Short

# 3. New Tools & Platforms

**Tool:** GitHub Copilot content exclusions (app and CLI)

**Category:** Engineering / Operations

**What does it do?**
Keeps selected files and paths out of Copilot context and suggestions.

**Who should use it?**
Technical leads who need agent use without exposing secrets, customer data or regulated code.

**Business Use Case:** A written, enforceable data boundary for AI coding tools.

**Estimated ROI:** Medium (risk reduction; cost is configuration time).

**Recommended Experiment:** Exclude secrets, env, customer-data and infra paths on one repo; confirm in the CLI that excluded files are not read.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 2 hours

---

**Tool:** Small-model router (any vendor's cheapest model, or Decisions API once generally available)

**Category:** AI / Operations

**What does it do?**
Sends classification and routing decisions to a cheap model and keeps expensive models for hard work.

**Who should use it?**
Anyone running an agent or support/triage workflow with measurable volume.

**Business Use Case:** Ticket triage, request routing, next-step selection in agent loops.

**Estimated ROI:** Medium-High if we have a high-volume decision step; unknown until measured.

**Recommended Experiment:** Take 200 past tickets or requests, label them by hand, and compare a cheap model against our current approach on accuracy and cost.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 0.5 day

---

**Tool:** Cloudflare Agent Memory (private beta, announced during Agents Week earlier this year)

**Category:** Cloud / Data

**What does it do?**
A managed service that stores what an agent should remember across sessions outside the context window.

**Who should use it?**
Teams building long-running assistants on Cloudflare.

**Business Use Case:** Persistent agent memory without building our own store.

**Estimated ROI:** Low now (private beta, announcement not new).

**Recommended Experiment:** None this month. Join the waitlist only if we build on Cloudflare.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 1 hour (reading)

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

1. **The agent runtime is being absorbed by the model vendors.** OpenAI now hosts the execution environment, Codex-style multi-agent features, and context handling. Anthropic (routines, mods) and Vercel (Agent Stack, announced earlier this year) are doing the same. What used to be our glue code is becoming a vendor feature.
2. **Price and model choice are moving fast and in our favor.** Near-flagship quality at one-fifth the price (GPT-6.1 Sol) and 75% cache-read cuts mean cost per task falls quarter by quarter. Contracts or architecture that assume today's prices will be wrong.
3. **Platforms are becoming multi-model.** Copilot, Notion (external agents) and others host several vendors' agents behind one interface. The value is shifting to the workflow and data boundary, not the model.
4. **Capital keeps flowing to the full stack** (agents, data, workflow), consistent with Temporal and Supabase on Oct 4. Funding is not evidence of fit for us.

**What This Means For Our Company**

- Do not build our own agent runtime or orchestration layer; buy or rent it and keep the logic that is ours (prompts, data, evaluation sets) portable.
- Create a small internal evaluation set of our own tasks. It is the one asset that lets us switch models and vendors on price or quality quickly.
- Review model and tool spend monthly; prices are dropping faster than contracts get renegotiated.
